target_customer: Individual online sellers on eBay, Amazon and Overstock
problem: Sellers had to list and manage items across several marketplaces by hand and lacked guidance on optimizing sales.
business_model: SaaS tool for marketplace sellers (pricing not found)
product_category: Multi-marketplace auction listing and sales management

founders.name: Harj Taggar
founders.background_notes: YC page says he founded it in college, later Triplebyte.

founders.name: Kulveer Taggar
founders.background_notes: Later founded Zeus per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Listing and sales management over marketplace interfaces; a two-to-four person team shipped it within a few months (Wikipedia describes the merge of Shuppa with the Taggars in 2007). Detailed technical evidence not found.

defensibility.rationale: No source shows any moat; listing tools were copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not found in sources read; the company was sold to Live Current Media in March 2008.

market_need_then: Well-known sellers on eBay and others needed bulk tools; no quantified spend found in sources read.

brand_strength.rationale: Name origin not stated in any source read; the name resembles an 'auto' plus '-matic' coinage but that is not sourced.

pivots.to: Auctomatic after merging with Harj and Kulveer Taggar and moving to California
pivots.why: Per Wikipedia; reason beyond the merge not stated.

outcome_analysis: Auctomatic was a small team in the Winter 2007 batch that built a multi-marketplace seller tool and was bought by Live Current Media in March 2008, within about a year of founding. The price and terms are not public in sources read, so whether this was a strong exit or a soft landing cannot be judged; the founders went on to Stripe and Triplebyte-type careers, which suggests founder quality rather than product scale was the main outcome.
notes: Funding: none found; Paul Buchheit invested per YC page and long description (amount unknown, not recorded as a round). Only YC page and Wikipedia were read; the Wikipedia article says the sale was on Good Friday 2008 without a price. Collison involvement with Stripe not verified here.
